chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, who linked it up to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him).

He said: The one who divulges (what others have said) has killed three people: he has killed himself, he has killed the one to whom he divulges what is said, and he has killed the one whose sayings he divulges.

key_terms.السَّاعِي: The one who divulges or spreads news/secrets
key_terms.قَاتِلُ مَنْ يَسْعَى إِلَيْهِ: He has killed the one whose words he repeats (the subject)
key_terms.قَاتِلُ مَنْ يَسْعَى بِهِ: He has killed the one to whom he speaks (the listener)
key_terms.قَاتِلُ نَفْسِهِ: He has killed himself (spiritually or literally)
key_terms.يَرْفَعُهُ: He links it up (to the Imam) via a chain of narrators

ai.seo_question: What are the three people killed by backbiting according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) profound metaphorical classification of backbiting as a tripartite 'killing': it slays the divulger’s own spiritual vitality, diminishes the status of the absent party, and kills the listener’s trust or peace of mind. This narration underscores the comprehensive social and spiritual damage of *ghibah*, extending beyond the individual to the communal fabric, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical jurisprudence.
